title: LeRobot v0.6.0: World-Model Policies for Robot Learning
hook: Hugging Face's open robotics library adds policies that imagine the future before acting, five new vision-language-action models, and a CLI for human-in-the-loop data collection.
key_points: Adds world-model policies that learn to imagine the future as part of training, alongside five new vision-language-action (VLA) models.
New unified reward-models API for success detection, plus six new simulation benchmarks and depth-camera support.
A new deployment CLI enables DAgger-style human-in-the-loop corrections for more efficient data collection.
Technical upgrades: FSDP multi-GPU training, cloud training via Hugging Face Jobs, and up to 2x faster dataset loading.
Lighter installation footprint and simplified APIs aim to make the framework more accessible to robotics newcomers.
content_html: Robot learning has historically meant stitching together separate tools for data collection, training, and evaluation. LeRobot v0.6.0 pushes toward a more complete, single pipeline.
extra_html: The release adds world-model policies — which learn to imagine the future as part of training rather than reacting only to the current frame — alongside five new vision-language-action models and a unified reward-models API for automatic success detection. Six new simulation benchmarks and comprehensive depth-camera support round out the evaluation side, while a new deployment CLI supports DAgger-style human-in-the-loop corrections, letting a human step in to correct a policy during deployment for more sample-efficient data collection than pure demonstrations. Under the hood, the release adds FSDP multi-GPU training, cloud training via Hugging Face Jobs, and up to 2x faster dataset loading, alongside a lighter installation footprint and simplified APIs meant to lower the barrier for newcomers exploring embodied AI. Hugging Face Blog, 2026-07-07.

related.title: World Action Models: A Survey
related.hook: Robots are learning to imagine the future before acting. This survey untangles 'world action models' from video generators and VLA policies — and finds them converging on one idea.
